# Parity fixture + golden snapshot (original k16)

Frozen inputs and the reference prediction snapshot that the `dlofeel-state`
port must reproduce. The golden was generated by the **original** `dlopredict`
repo (never the port), so it fixes the target before any code is ported.

## What is here

| File | Role |
|------|------|
| `samples/<session>/sample_*.h5` | 8 frozen c1-test frames (the fixture inputs) |
| `config.yaml` | The k16 checkpoint's own config (model architecture + eval knobs) |
| `golden_preds.h5` | Original repo's predictions on the 8 frames (the parity target) |

The k16 `best.pt` (137 MB) is **never committed**. It is referenced by env var
(see below) and will be HF-hosted in Phase 3.

## Fixture identity

- Dataset: c1 test set (the primary DLO the k16 model was trained on),
  on the FAST_DATA mount `/media/rotem/FAST_DATA/dlopredict_data/c1/ds/test`.
- Session (first, deterministic `ls | sort | head -1`): `01_13_14_46_deg115`
- Samples (first 8, deterministic `ls sample_*.h5 | sort | head -8`):
  `sample_0, sample_1000, sample_1001, sample_1002, sample_1003, sample_1004,
  sample_1005, sample_1006`
- Total size: 7.2 MB (8 x ~913 KB), under the 10 MB fixture budget.

The `<session>/` subdir is preserved so the dataset loader's recursive
directory walk (`os.walk`) discovers the frames exactly as in the full set.
The loader sorts by `(session, int(sample_N))`, so within the fixture the
temporal order is `sample_0` then `sample_1000..1006`.

## Exact command that produced `golden_preds.h5`

Run from the ORIGINAL repo root (`norm_stats_path` inside the checkpoint config
is repo-relative, so cwd must be the original repo). `evaluate.py` auto-loads
the config sitting next to `best.pt`; there is no `--config_path` /
`--norm_stats_path` flag (those were removed from the argparse). All eval knobs
(num_output_pts 16, with_att, use_diff_images, use_blank_ref, single_encoder,
normalize, normalize_inputs) come from that config.

```bash
ORIG=/home/rotem/Documents/Claude/Projects/PHD/03_projects/dlopredict/repo
NEW=/home/rotem/Documents/Claude/Projects/PHD/03_projects/dlopredict/dlofeel-state
cd "$ORIG"
export PYTHONPATH="src:${PYTHONPATH:-}"
uv run python src/simplepredict/evaluate.py \
  --ckpt results/ral_bigrun/k_resample_ablation/k16/checkpoints/k16/best.pt \
  --data_root "$NEW/tests/fixtures/parity/samples" \
  --blank_ref_root src/datasets/ds/digit_blank_closed_refs \
  --out_dir /tmp/parity_golden \
  --batch_size 8
# then: cp /tmp/parity_golden/k16/preds_gts.h5 $NEW/tests/fixtures/parity/golden_preds.h5
```

- `--blank_ref_root src/datasets/ds/digit_blank_closed_refs` matches the path
  the k16 training used (serials D21118, D21122, D21123, D21124); `use_blank_ref`
  is true so these PNGs are the diff-image background.
- Device: CUDA (NVIDIA RTX 5090), torch 2.10.0+cu128. The config's
  `deterministic: false`, so cross-device / cross-run reproduction should be
  compared with a tolerance, not bit-exact.

## Parity target (this fixture's aggregate, denormalized mm)

Recorded from the original run's `run_metrics.json` (`aggregate`), n=8:

| Metric | Value (mm) |
|--------|-----------|
| RMSE (l2_mean)     | 34.00 |
| RMSE std (l2_std)  | 22.30 |
| Chamfer mean       | 29.46 |
| Chamfer std        | 12.20 |

This is the fixture's own number and does NOT equal the full-test 30.52 mm
(30.52 is over the entire c1 test set; this is an 8-frame subset). Per-sample
RMSE (m): `sample_0` = 0.0928 (temporally isolated, so its past-frame falls back
to a velocity-0 duplicate, inflating its error), the other seven = 0.021 to
0.027. 7/8 are below the 0.055 low-RMSE threshold.

`golden_preds.h5` datasets: `preds (8,16,3)`, `gts (8,16,3)`, `poses (8,7)`,
`losses (8,)`, `sample_paths (8,)` (all denormalized; float32).

## Checkpoint env-var convention

The k16 weights are not in git. Parity-test executors export the path to
`best.pt` before running:

```bash
export DLOFEEL_PARITY_CKPT=$ORIG/results/ral_bigrun/k_resample_ablation/k16/checkpoints/k16/best.pt
```

Phase 3 replaces this local path with a Hugging Face-hosted download; the `.pt`
is never committed to this repo under any circumstance.
